newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends mixed on heavy liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends mixed on heavy liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended mixed in active trading on Friday, with both long and short position holders liquidating their positions in the September 1996 contract, traders said.

The key September 1996 contract ended at 2,400 yuan ($289) per tonne, losing 78 yuan. It opened limit-down at 2,388 and hit an intra-day high of 2,410. The settlement price was 2,397, down from Thursday's 2,467.
The settlement prices are weighted average prices of all contracts transacted on the day and the limit-up and limit-down are calculated according to settlement prices.
October rose 28 yuan to 2,342 yuan with a settlement price of 2,334 yuan, up from 2,320.
Combined volume rose sharply to 126,700 tonnes from 5,200.

Traders said both long and short position holders were eager to offset their positions in the September contract on the approach of its delivery date next Tuesday, making it fall sharply on dramatically higher volume.
"Long position holders had to offset their positions and sustain heavy losses because they did not want to take physical goods," one trader said.
"The open interest of the September contract fell sharply, indicating institutional sellers were willing to cash in their positions," he added.
The open interest of the September contract fell to 3,110 lots from 15,330. One lot is five tonnes of rice.
Traders expect rice contracts to move only slightly early next week, with most investors having no positions in hand.
